reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds an isNonWorkingDay predicate, threading holidays to every existing caller, but getDatesInRange re-codes its own non-working-day check instead of using that predicate.

duplication.why: The daily-skip rule is implemented separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange, the holiday check is re-coded in getDatesInRange (holidays?.includes, which already diverges by missing MM-DD entries), and the handler copies getUpcomingDates' RSchedule/try-catch skeleton.

placement.why: The moving loop and predicate live in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip decision is embedded in getNextDate and the server handler rather than in one shared rule, and isNonWorkingDay is kept private so the server cannot reuse it.

scope.why: Edits stay within the schedule date logic, the new handler, the type and parse plumbing and tests.

maintainability.why: Holiday matching already exists in two forms that disagree (recurring MM-DD only honoured in the shared predicate), and the daily rule is absent from getUpcomingDates and the budget template, so the rule is hard to change safely.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange checks d.isWeekend(date) || config.holidays?.includes(...) itself instead of the isNonWorkingDay predicate used by getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The non-working-day predicate is reshaped in getDatesInRange as an inline includes() test, and the daily skip appears as a filter in getNextDate and as a flatMap returning [] in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains the isDailyWithSkippedWeekends special case; getDatesInRange re-implements the predicate and daily skip; getUpcomingDates and schedule-template.ts apply only the move rule, not the daily skip.
